sources.title: FIXTURE — Headwall Flashing Practice Note (fictional trade association)

passages.quote: Where a metal roof terminates against a masonry wall, an apron flashing turned up the wall at least 150 mm shall be covered by a separate counterflashing.
passages.claim: At a headwall, an apron flashing turned up the wall is covered by a separate counterflashing.

passages.quote: A surface-mounted counterflashing must be mechanically fixed and sealed; it shall not rely on sealant alone.
passages.claim: Surface-held counterflashing is acceptable when mechanically fixed and sealed, not sealant alone.

passages.quote: A reglet is a groove cut into a bed joint to receive the counterflashing; cutting requires the masonry to be sound.
passages.claim: Reglet counterflashing needs a sound bed joint that may be cut.

sources.title: FIXTURE — Cavity Wall Drainage Bulletin (synthetic building-science note)

passages.quote: In a cavity wall, water that enters the outer leaf must be intercepted by a cavity tray above the roof abutment and discharged through weep holes.
passages.claim: A cavity wall needs a through-wall cavity tray with weeps above a roof abutment.

passages.quote: Surface-applied counterflashing on a cavity wall does not stop water already inside the cavity and should not be relied on as the only defence.
passages.claim: Surface-held counterflashing is acceptable when mechanically fixed and sealed, not sealant alone.
